## Definitions

- [statement] The locked percentage is a legacy global write-lock field that appears only against MongoDB versions before 3.0. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them

## How it works

- [statement] mongostat normalizes operation statistics to average operations per second even when the polling interval exceeds one second. Read operation rates separately from connection counts and memory snapshots. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] mongostat set gives the replica-set name when applicable; repl gives member state: PRI primary, SEC secondary, REC recovering, UNK unknown, RTR mongos router, and ARB arbiter. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] mongostat --discover can return statistics for all members when connected to a sharded cluster through mongos; the examples also combine --discover with --interactive for a non-scrolling view. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat/mongostat-examples.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] CloudThinker uses mongotop as a per-collection, per-interval workload view and separates queued readers/writers from active readers/writers when reading mongostat. (low confidence) — https://cloudthinker.io/blogs/mongodb-performance-audit-native-tools · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] mongostat vsize reports process virtual memory and res reports process resident memory, documented in megabytes at the last call. conn reports the total number of open connections. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] For WiredTiger, flushes counts checkpoints triggered between polling intervals. This field is an interval count rather than a checkpoint-duration measurement. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] vsize reports process virtual memory, whereas res reports process resident memory. The reference describes these as memory amounts at the last mongostat call, rather than operation rates. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them · also: https://genexdbs.com/introduction-to-mongodb-diagnostic-tools-mongotop-and-mongostat/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] mongostat gives an instance-level status overview; mongotop locates read and write activity at the collection level. Use the two views together to relate node pressure to busy collections. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop.md, https://software.danielwatrous.com/mongodb-monitoring-with-mongostat/
- [statement] The operation columns report inserts, query operations, updates, deletes, cursor-batch getmore operations, and commands per second. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them · also: https://genexdbs.com/introduction-to-mongodb-diagnostic-tools-mongotop-and-mongostat/
- [statement] An asterisk on the insert value denotes a replicated operation. On a secondary, command values separated by a pipe represent local|replicated commands. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] For WiredTiger, dirty is tracked dirty bytes divided by maximum configured cache bytes; used is current cache bytes divided by maximum configured cache bytes. Both are cache percentages, so interpret them against the configured WiredTiger cache. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] mongostat qr and qw are queue lengths for clients waiting to read and write; ar and aw count active clients performing reads and writes. The paired output headings qrw and arw distinguish queued from active readers and writers. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them · also: https://cloudthinker.io/blogs/mongodb-performance-audit-native-tools, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat/mongostat-examples.md
- [statement] netIn and netOut measure incoming and outgoing network traffic in bytes, including traffic generated by mongostat itself; conn is the total number of open connections. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] mongotop time values are milliseconds. ns combines database and collection names; total is time spent operating on the namespace, while read and write report time spent performing the respective operations. The timestamp dates the returned data. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them · also: https://genexdbs.com/introduction-to-mongodb-diagnostic-tools-mongotop-and-mongostat/
- [statement] mongotop reports active namespaces or databases. If a collection or database is absent, the documentation says it has received no recent activity. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] mongotop --json adds operation counts for the polling interval to the timing data. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] mongotop --locks is historical: it reports per-database locks only for MongoDB 2.6 or older and errors on 3.0 or newer instances that do not expose that data. In this mode db replaces ns, and database name . denotes the global lock. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] mongostat -o selects the output columns; -O adds serverStatus fields after the defaults. The options are mutually exclusive. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat/mongostat-examples.md
- [statement] For custom numerical serverStatus columns, .rate() reports the per-second change and .diff() reports change since the previous sample. The official examples demonstrate both in the -o field expression. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat/mongostat-examples.md
- [statement] The historical Stack Overflow discussion cautions that operation-rate interpretation depends on the server configuration and cluster architecture; its example throughput numbers are not universal capacity limits. (low confidence) — https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13522241/interpreting-mongostat-and-mongotop-output · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] The mongostat inserts field counts inserted objects per second; query, update and delete count operations per second. getmore counts cursor-batch operations per second. An asterisk after an insert value denotes a replicated operation; secondary command values use local|replicated. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] mongostat netIn and netOut describe received and sent network traffic in bytes, including traffic generated by mongostat itself. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them
- [statement] mongotop reports read and write activity per collection and accepts a reporting interval in seconds; its default reporting interval is one second. Use its per-collection view to locate where read and write time is concentrated. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them · also: https://cloudthinker.io/blogs/mongodb-performance-audit-native-tools
- [statement] Historical lock fields need server-version context: mongostat locked appears only for pre-3.0 servers. mongotop --locks needs MongoDB 2.6 or older and errors on MongoDB 3.0 or newer servers that do not report per-database lock usage. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongostat.md · keywords: mongostat and mongotop fields and how to read them · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongotop.md
